name: Takoyaki (Octopus Balls)
instructions: Mix flour and dashi into a smooth batter.
Heat takoyaki pan, oil well, pour batter halfway.
Add octopus, green onion, ginger, and tenkasu.
Turn balls carefully with picks until round and golden.
Top with sauce, mayo, bonito flakes, and aonori.
tips: A proper takoyaki pan makes all the difference — a round pan won’t work well.

name: Okonomiyaki (Savory Cabbage Pancake)
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, and dashi into a batter.
Add shredded cabbage and mix well.
Pour onto a hot oiled pan and shape into a thick pancake.
Cook until both sides are golden.
Top with okonomiyaki sauce, mayonnaise, and bonito flakes.
tips: Add tenkasu (tempura bits) or thinly sliced pork for extra flavor and texture.

name: Korokke (Japanese Croquettes)
instructions: Sauté onion and ground meat, then mix into mashed potatoes.
Shape into oval patties and chill for 20 minutes.
Coat with flour → egg → panko.
Deep-fry until golden and crispy.
Serve with tonkatsu sauce or Worcestershire sauce.
tips: Chilling the shaped korokke helps them hold their shape while frying.

name: Taiyaki (Fish-shaped Cake)
instructions: Make a smooth pancake-like batter.
Heat and oil the taiyaki pan.
Pour a little batter, add filling, then cover with more batter.
Cook until both sides are golden.
Serve warm.
tips: Red bean paste is classic, but chocolate or cheese fillings are popular modern variations.

name: Edamame with Sea Salt

ingredients.name: Frozen or fresh edamame in pods

instructions: Boil or steam the edamame pods for 3–5 minutes until bright green.
Drain well.
Toss with sea salt while still hot.
Serve immediately as a simple snack.
tips: A classic izakaya snack — very easy and healthy.

name: Karaage (Japanese Fried Chicken Bites)
instructions: Marinate chicken in soy, ginger, garlic, and sake for 15–30 minutes.
Coat lightly in potato starch.
Deep-fry until golden and crispy.
Drain and serve with lemon and Japanese mayo.
tips: Double-frying makes them extra crispy. Perfect party snack.

name: Spring Rolls
instructions: Prepare fillings and lay out wrappers.
Add fillings, fold and roll tightly.
Deep-fry until golden (or serve fresh).
Serve with dipping sauce.
tips: For fresh spring rolls, use rice paper and don’t fry.

name: Sesame Balls (Jian Dui)
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour, sugar, and water into a soft dough.
Divide dough, flatten, and fill with red bean paste.
Roll into balls and coat thoroughly with sesame seeds.
Deep-fry on medium heat until golden and puffed.
Drain and serve warm.
tips: Fry on medium heat so the inside cooks fully without burning the sesame seeds.

name: Egg Tarts
instructions: Press pastry into mini tart molds.
Whisk eggs, sugar, evaporated milk, and vanilla.
Strain the custard and fill the shells.
Bake at 200°C until the custard is set and pastry is golden.
Cool slightly before serving.
tips: These are perfect as a sweet merienda or afternoon snack.

name: Turnip Cake Bites (pan-fried)
instructions: Cook daikon, mix with rice flour and seasonings, steam until set.
Cool, slice into small pieces.
Pan-fry until golden and crispy on the outside.
Serve with chili sauce as a snack.
tips: Small bite-sized pieces make this perfect for snacking instead of a full meal.

name: Prawn Toast
instructions: Mix minced shrimp with egg white, cornstarch, and ginger.
Spread thickly on bread slices, press sesame seeds on top.
Deep-fry or pan-fry until golden and cooked through.
Cut into triangles and serve hot.
tips: A classic Chinese restaurant appetizer that works great as a party snack.

name: Sweet Potato Balls
instructions: Mix mashed sweet potato with glutinous rice flour and sugar.
Shape into small balls.
Deep-fry until golden and slightly puffed.
Optional: roll in sesame seeds while hot.
Serve warm.
tips: Chewy outside, soft and sweet inside — a popular street snack.

name: Korean Corn Dogs (Gamja Hotdog)
instructions: Make a slightly sweet yeast batter and let it rise.
Skewer sausages/mozzarella, dip in batter, then roll in panko.
Deep-fry until golden and puffed.
Roll in sugar while hot (classic Korean style).
Serve with ketchup and mustard.
tips: For the popular ‘potato’ version, roll the battered dog in thin potato sticks before frying.

name: Hotteok (Sweet Filled Pancakes)
instructions: Make a soft dough with flour, yeast, sugar, and warm milk. Rest 40–50 minutes.
Divide dough, fill with brown sugar-cinnamon-nut mixture, and seal.
Flatten gently and pan-fry in oil until both sides are golden.
Press lightly while cooking so the sugar melts inside.
Serve hot (be careful of the molten filling).
tips: These are a classic Korean street snack — best eaten fresh and hot.

name: Gimmari (Fried Seaweed Rolls)
instructions: Cook glass noodles, season with soy and sesame oil, mix with vegetables.
Roll tightly in nori sheets.
Cut into bite-sized pieces and deep-fry until crispy.
Serve with a simple soy-vinegar dip.
tips: A popular Korean street snack, often served with tteokbokki.

name: Twigim (Korean Fried Vegetables & Seafood)

ingredients.name: Frying batter mix or flour + egg + water

instructions: Cut vegetables and seafood into pieces.
Coat in batter.
Deep-fry until golden and crispy.
Serve hot with dipping sauce.
tips: Often sold together with tteokbokki at Korean street stalls.

name: Sundae (Korean Blood Sausage)

ingredients.name: Pork blood + glass noodles + glutinous rice
Optional: perilla leaves or green chili

instructions: Mix the filling ingredients thoroughly.
Stuff into cleaned casings and tie the ends.
Steam or boil for 30–40 minutes until firm.
Slice into rounds and serve warm.
Eat with salted shrimp sauce or a simple soy-vinegar dip.
tips: A classic Korean street snack, often sold alongside tteokbokki. The store-bought version is very convenient.

name: Kimchi Jeon (Kimchi Pancake)
instructions: Mix chopped kimchi with flour, egg, and a little water into a thick batter.
Pan-fry in a generous amount of oil until crispy on both sides.
Cut into pieces and serve with dipping sauce.
tips: Use well-fermented kimchi for the best flavor. Great rainy-day snack.

name: Lumpia Shanghai
instructions: Mix ground pork with carrots, onions, and seasonings.
Wrap mixture tightly in lumpia wrappers.
Seal edges with water or egg wash.
Deep fry until golden brown and crispy.
Serve with sweet chili sauce.
tips: Roll them tightly to prevent oil from seeping inside.

name: Kwek-Kwek (Orange Battered Quail Eggs)

ingredients.name: Annatto powder or orange food coloring

instructions: Make a thick orange-colored batter with flour, annatto, and water.
Dip each peeled quail egg into the batter.
Deep-fry until the coating is crispy and bright orange.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve with sweet-spicy vinegar dipping sauce.
tips: A very popular Filipino street merienda — usually sold on skewers.

name: Banana Cue
instructions: Heat oil and add brown sugar until it starts to melt.
Add whole saba bananas and fry, coating them in the caramelizing sugar.
Turn until evenly coated and deep golden.
Skewer 2–3 bananas per stick.
Serve hot as a classic street merienda.
tips: The sugar creates a shiny, crunchy caramel shell — very addictive.

name: Fish Balls with Sauce
instructions: Deep-fry or boil the fish balls until cooked and slightly browned.
Serve on skewers or in a small bowl.
Offer sweet sauce and spicy vinegar on the side.
Classic street-style merienda.
tips: A true Filipino street food staple — cheap, filling, and perfect for afternoon snacks.

name: Ukoy (Shrimp Fritters)
instructions: Mix vegetables and shrimp with the batter.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and flatten slightly.
Fry until crispy and golden.
Serve with garlic-vinegar dip.
tips: Crispy on the outside, full of shrimp and vegetables inside — a classic merienda.

name: Puto (Steamed Rice Cakes)
instructions: Mix rice flour, sugar, baking powder, and liquid into a smooth batter.
Pour into small molds.
Top with cheese or salted egg if desired.
Steam for 15–20 minutes until set.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: Often eaten with dinuguan, but also perfect on its own as a soft, mildly sweet snack.

name: Thai Fish Cakes (Tod Mun Pla)
instructions: Blend fish with curry paste, fish sauce, and egg until sticky.
Mix in long beans and kaffir lime leaves.
Shape into small flat cakes.
Deep-fry until golden and puffed.
Serve with sweet chili sauce and cucumber relish.
tips: The mixture should be sticky — this helps the cakes hold together and become bouncy.

name: Satay Chicken Skewers
instructions: Marinate chicken in coconut milk and spices for at least 20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill until cooked and slightly charred.
Serve with peanut sauce and cucumber relish.
tips: A classic Thai snack or appetizer — the peanut sauce is essential.

name: Por Pia Tod (Thai Fried Spring Rolls)
instructions: Cook and season the filling, then cool.
Wrap tightly in spring roll wrappers.
Deep-fry until golden and crispy.
Serve with sweet chili sauce.
tips: Make sure the filling is not too wet so the rolls stay crispy.

name: Khao Tom Mat (Banana Sticky Rice in Leaves)
instructions: Mix sticky rice with sweetened coconut milk.
Place rice and banana on banana leaf, wrap tightly.
Steam for 40–45 minutes.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: A traditional Thai snack often sold at markets — fragrant from the banana leaf.

name: Mieng Kham (Leaf-wrapped Bites)
instructions: Arrange small amounts of each filling on a leaf.
Drizzle with a little palm sugar syrup.
Wrap and eat in one bite.
The mix of sweet, salty, sour, spicy, and crunchy is the point.
tips: A refined Thai snack that hits every flavor at once.

name: Thai Iced Tea Pudding Cups
instructions: Brew strong Thai tea and strain.
Mix with coconut milk, sugar, and agar-agar.
Pour into small cups and let set.
Optional: top with a layer of sweetened milk.
Chill and serve as a refreshing snack.
tips: A modern Thai café-style snack that is easy to make at home.
